meta.title: Mia's Photos
meta.textType: story told as an email for a clear reader

paragraphs: Subject: My photos from the cooking class. Dear Nadia, Hello from Thailand! First, a small thing about my kitten Snow. She sleeps on my bed every night, and she is well. This week, I took photos at a cooking class, and I want to tell you about it. I know that you love photography too.

On Saturday, the Explorers went to a cooking class in a small kitchen near the market. It was a hot morning, so we stayed indoors. Chef Lucy met us at the door in her white apron. The kitchen smelled of sweet fruit, and a long table stood in the middle. First, we washed our hands with soap. We made a fruit salad and sweet rice cakes. Teacher Kim gave me the club camera. It is a digital camera with a big screen, and the technology is new. I am the photographer of the Explorers, but I did not take a photo at first.

I was shy, because I did not know Chef Lucy. I stood in the corner and held the camera in both hands. Leo put flour on his nose, and everybody laughed, but I did not click. The room was loud, and the children talked and laughed. Chef Lucy looked at me and smiled. "A good photographer waits for the right moment," she said. "Do not hide behind the camera. Watch, and then click."

So I watched. Chef Lucy cut the fruit into small pieces, and her hands moved very fast. May put the rice cakes in a pot, and steam came up. I clicked, and the photo was good. Then Leo laughed with flour on his nose, and there was steam behind him. I clicked again, and this is my favorite photo of the day. Lily asked me to show her the photo, and I held the screen near her. Lily wrote notes in her notebook, and I took a photo of her too. Chef Lucy looked at the screen and said, "That is a good photo."

Teacher Kim will put three photos on Explorers' Blog. What do you like to take photos of, Nadia? Please send me a photo of an animal. Do you have a cooking class at school in Singapore? I hope that you can see the photos soon. Your friend, Mia.
text.summary: Mia writes an email to her pen pal Nadia about a cooking class. She is shy at first, and Chef Lucy tells her to wait for the right moment and then click.
